query: To quantify how visual cue intensity affects HD encoding accuracy across the population, compute HD encoding accuracy for each of 15 flies under no-cue, dim-cue, and bright-cue conditions, using movement periods only and defining accuracy as one minus circular variance of the EPG bump-phase-to-head-direction offset. Compare the three cue conditions as repeated measurements across flies, report pairwise statistical comparisons, and visualize the result as a paired within-fly connected-line plot: each fly is shown as a thin gray line connecting its values across the three conditions, the population mean is overlaid as a thick black line, and pairwise P values are annotated above the condition comparisons.

analyse_plan.Objective: Compare HD encoding accuracy across three visual cue intensity conditions at the population level.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify that HD encoding accuracy is computed only during periods of fly movement; confirm circular variance calculated correctly over each 200-s block; confirm appropriate statistical model (fly as random effect). HD encoding accuracy is computed as 1 - circular variance of the EPG bump-phase relative to HD.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load the EPG ΔF/F traces, the FicTrac-derived HD time series (rotational-velocity integral on the 9-mm foam ball with 0.2–0.3 L min⁻¹ airflow), the 200-s block labels (no cue, dim cue, bright cue) for all 15 flies, and the per-frame immobility annotations. 2. Preprocess Imaging: Apply NoRMCorre rigid x/y/z motion correction to each fly's two-photon volume series (256×128 pixels, 12 z-slices at 5-µm spacing, 9.18 volumes per second), draw the PB mask from the maximum z-projection, divide the PB into 25–40 ROIs along a polyline midline, and compute per-ROI ΔF/F with the 10th-percentile fluorescence as the trial-by-ROI baseline F. 3. Fit Bump Position Per Frame: Fit a von Mises function f(x) = α·exp(κ·cos(x − µ)) + c to each timepoint with Matlab's nonlinear-least-squares fit (trust-region algorithm); take µ as the bump position. 4. Apply Quality Filtering: Discard timepoints with adjusted R² < 0.5 and timepoints flagged as immobile from the encoding-accuracy computation. 5. Compute Per-Block Offsets: For each fly and each 200-s block, compute offset = bump_position − (−HD) at every retained timepoint. 6. Compute Per-Block HD Encoding Accuracy: For each fly and each block, treat each offset value as a unit vector and compute the resultant vector strength; define HD encoding accuracy as 1 − circular variance = vector strength. 7. Run Across-Block Statistics: Across the 15 flies, compare HD encoding accuracy among the no-cue, dim-cue, and bright-cue blocks using linear mixed-effects models with Tukey post-hoc comparisons and Bonferroni corrections, with fly identity as a random effect. 8. Save Key Results: Save the per-fly per-block HD encoding accuracy values, the across-fly mean per condition, and the linear-mixed-effects-model statistics with Tukey-Bonferroni P values used for the panel. 9. Visualization: Plot per-fly HD encoding accuracy across the three conditions (no cue, dim cue, bright cue) with single flies as gray lines, the across-fly mean as a thick black line, and the Tukey-Bonferroni P values annotated above the across-condition comparison brackets.

key_analysis_results: In 15 flies, HD encoding accuracy progressively increased with visual cue intensity. All pairwise comparisons were statistically significant (no cue vs. dim cue P = 3.87e-5; no cue vs. bright cue P = 2e-8; dim cue vs. bright cue P < 1e-15; linear mixed-effects models with Tukey comparisons and Bonferroni corrections).
key_analysis_conclusions: Increasing visual cue intensity produces graded improvement in the accuracy of HD encoding in the Drosophila HD system, demonstrating that brighter cues convey more information to the ring attractor network.

summary_report.abstract: HD encoding accuracy was compared across three cue intensity conditions at the population level.
summary_report.methods: EPG calcium imaging (jGCaMP7f) in 15 flies, 200-s interleaved blocks, HD encoding accuracy = 1 - circular variance. Statistics: linear mixed-effects models with Tukey and Bonferroni.
summary_report.results: All pairwise comparisons significant: no cue vs. dim P = 3.87e-5, no cue vs. bright P = 2e-8, dim vs. bright P < 1e-15.
summary_report.discussion: Foundational result establishing graded improvement of HD encoding accuracy with cue intensity.
